analysis.title: "Long-Term Constructive, Just Not Today": Goldman Cuts Gold Target Again As Warsh Kills The "Debasement" Trade (For Now)
key_insights: Goldman lowered its end-2026 gold forecast to $4,150/toz from $4,650 and its end-2027 forecast to $4,800/toz from $5,400. Spot gold was about $4,130 on Thursday morning, so the new year-end target implies roughly no move over the next eight weeks.

This is a string of cuts. In June the December 2026 target went to $4,900 from $5,400 after the first Fed meeting under Chair Warsh, then to $4,650, and now $4,150. The record near $5,600 was in January.

Goldman assumes central bank buying of 60 tonnes a month through 2026-27. The seasonally adjusted three-month average is 85 tonnes a month and the pre-2022 average was 17 tonnes. Central bank demand drives most of the 15% price upside Goldman forecasts by end-2027.

Goldman expects macro-policy hedge demand (call-option demand) and gold ETFs to subtract from the price path. Its base case assumes the Fed's hawkish shift and a December 2026 hike keep investor debasement concerns contained, so call demand normalizes toward its historical average.

FOMC held at 3.75%-4.00% in a 10-2 vote, with Hammack and Governor Cook dissenting in favor of a hike. Goldman economists give 50% to two hikes followed by cuts to 3.25%-3.5%, 35% to three hikes and a higher terminal rate, and 15% to recession.

Under the three-hike scenario Goldman's model puts gold at $4,660/toz by end-2027, versus the $4,800 base case. Risks skew lower: an additional March 2027 hike, delayed cuts, or a higher terminal rate.
Goldman frames this as a repeat of 2022, when higher rates weighed on investor positioning but gold held up better than real yields implied because of the central bank bid.

Goldman's model says 100 tonnes of net conviction demand raises gold about 2%, and a 1 million contract increase in net GLD call open interest adds roughly 5%. Dealer hedging of sold calls amplifies moves in both directions. Net GLD call open interest is about 1.9 million contracts versus a historical average near 1.0 million. Goldman left this amplification out of its base case, citing the short history of elevated call demand.

For CTAs and macro hedge funds, the next 3-6 months stay challenging because of higher rates, inflation and labor data volatility, tight drawdown limits, possibly higher oil and systematic selling. Sharp equity drawdowns could pull gold lower initially through margin calls.

For longer-horizon investors Goldman says the current correction may offer a more attractive entry point. Upside returns once the Fed starts easing in 2027H2, with three cuts expected from late 2027 through early 2028. The call-demand upside scenario tops out above $6,000.

Goldman's trading desk differs from its strategists. Rich Privorotsky said gold has become an inverse oil trade, making long gold potentially a more defensible de-escalation trade than short oil. Adam Gillard said Goldman's CTA model is close to max short with the pain trade likely higher, a day after gold's biggest daily gain since August.

The ZeroHedge author notes the base case rests on a December hike that markets doubt. Per Simon White, leveraged funds' net long in fed funds futures is the highest since 2020, with the Nasdaq in a correction. The author's own view is that the Fed blinks before 2027H2.

risk_factors: Further Fed hikes, including an additional March 2027 hike, delayed cuts or a higher terminal rate.
Higher oil prices adding to systematic selling in gold.
Sharp equity drawdowns triggering margin calls and deleveraging that pull gold lower initially.
Dealer unwinding of call hedges amplifying downside if call open interest keeps falling.
CTAs and macro funds face tight drawdown limits that make long gold positions hard to hold.
vol_and_positioning: Net GLD call open interest is about 1.9 million contracts versus a historical average near 1.0 million. Goldman estimates a 1 million contract change moves gold about 5%.
Dealers that sold calls may buy gold to hedge as price nears strikes, reinforcing rallies, and unwind hedges on declines, amplifying downside.
Goldman's CTA model is close to max short in gold, with the pain trade likely higher (Adam Gillard).
Goldman noted $19.5 billion of speculative gold futures selling over five straight weeks before the $4,000 break, when gold fell 5.4% on a day yields and the dollar were lower.
Leveraged funds' net long in fed funds futures is the highest since 2020 (Simon White, via ZeroHedge).
geopolitical: Iran war: EM central banks sold gold to pay for higher energy bills, per the ZeroHedge author.
Tuesday's Democratic sweep and a fiscal outlook that is not tightening, per the author.
Higher military spending and rising debt burdens in energy-importing countries could revive fiscal worries and call demand, per Goldman.

tension_points.bull_case: Central bank buying at 85 tonnes a month versus 17 pre-2022, CTA positioning close to max short with the pain trade higher (Gillard), and Fed easing from 2027H2 support a rebound. Goldman sees about 15% upside by end-2027.
tension_points.bear_case: A December hike and further hikes keep debasement hedge demand contained, call open interest normalizes from 1.9 million toward 1.0 million contracts, and CTAs and macro funds struggle to hold longs for 3-6 months.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A Fed that does not hike in December, which the ZeroHedge author argues is increasingly priced by markets, would undercut Goldman's base case for contained debasement demand.
